> **Pipeline step 05 — maps.**
>
> **Purpose.** The edge-type map (one panel per TPS edge class) and the TPS/EDSM water-body map,
> drawn on a TIGERweb vector water basemap (downloaded and cached on first run; see also
> `00_data/00_download_web_data.R`).
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv`, `data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv`,
> `data/All_Surveys_Combined_v7.3.csv` (Rip Rap reference tows only),
> `data/spatial/delta_hydro_tiger.rds`.
> **Outputs.** `output_figs/TPS_edge_type_map.*`, `output_figs/TPS_EDSM_waterbody_map.*`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Two journal-format figures built from the modelled tow data
(`data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv`, `data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv`):

* **`TPS_edge_type_map.*`** — 174 mm wide, six faceted panels (one per edge type),
  8 pt type throughout, in-panel corner labels, hairline black dividers.
* **`TPS_EDSM_waterbody_map.*`** — 84 mm wide, TPS over EDSM, shared extent,
  single shared legend inside the bottom panel.

Both are sized so the panels fill the stated width exactly: the figure height is
derived from the map's own aspect ratio, so there are no white letterbox bands
on the sides.

Rip Rap tows come from `data/All_Surveys_Combined_v7.3.csv` rather than the model
data — all 8 were dropped when the modelling dataset was built (none of their
station codes or coordinates appear in `tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv`). They are
mapped in the last panel for reference only; note this in the figure caption.

The basemap is vector (TIGER/Line areal hydrography: white water on grey land)
rather than a raster tile service — CARTO's keyless tiles are now watermarked,
and a vector basemap is reproducible offline and carries no tile-attribution
requirement for publication. It is downloaded once and cached to `data/spatial/`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(patchwork)

dir.create("output_figs",  showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("data/spatial", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

BASE_PT <- 8                 # every piece of text in both figures
PT_MM   <- BASE_PT / .pt     # same size expressed for geom_label()
```

```{r basemap, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# TIGERweb areal hydrography for the Suisun Bay / west Delta study area.
# Downloaded once, then read from the local cache.
HYDRO_RDS <- "data/spatial/delta_hydro_tiger.rds"
BBOX      <- c(xmin = -122.60, ymin = 37.92, xmax = -121.68, ymax = 38.32)

if (!file.exists(HYDRO_RDS)) {
  url <- paste0(
    "https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/Hydro/",
    "MapServer/1/query?",
    "geometry=", paste(BBOX[c("xmin", "ymin", "xmax", "ymax")], collapse = ","),
    "&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&outSR=4326",
    "&spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects&where=1%3D1&outFields=NAME",
    "&returnGeometry=true&f=geojson"
  )
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
  utils::download.file(url, tmp, quiet = TRUE)
  h <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_read(tmp, quiet = TRUE))
  h <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_crop(h, BBOX))
  h <- sf::st_geometry(h)          # geometry only; attributes unused
  saveRDS(h, HYDRO_RDS)
}
hydro <- readRDS(HYDRO_RDS)

LAND_FILL  <- "#dcdcdc"   # cartolight-like grey land
WATER_FILL <- "#ffffff"

# Water drawn with no stroke: TIGER splits polygons at county lines, and an
# outline would show those seams as spurious lines across San Pablo Bay.
basemap_layer <- function() geom_sf(data = hydro, fill = WATER_FILL, colour = NA)
```

```{r palette}
# Okabe-Ito / CUD palette, as specified.
pal <- c(
  "Shoal"                = "#0072B2",   # water body AND edge level share this colour
  "Distributary Channel" = "#56B4E9",
  "Terminal Channel"     = "#CC79A7",
  "Natural Edge"         = "#000000",
  "Emergent Vegetation"  = "#009E73",
  "Earthen Levee"        = "#D55E00",
  "Cut Bank"             = "#F0E442",
  "Rip Rap"              = "#E69F00"
)

darken <- function(hex, f = 0.55) {
  m <- col2rgb(hex) * f
  rgb(m[1, ], m[2, ], m[3, ], maxColorValue = 255)
}
pal_stroke <- setNames(darken(pal), names(pal))
pal_stroke["Cut Bank"] <- "#8a7a00"   # pale yellow needs a stronger edge on white water
```

```{r load, message=FALSE}
recode_wb <- function(x) recode(x,
  "Shoal"        = "Shoal",
  "Distributary" = "Distributary Channel",
  "Terminal"     = "Terminal Channel")

tps <- read_csv("data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(waterbody = recode_wb(habitat2020),
         edge = recode(Edge_Type,
                       "Open Shoal"          = "Shoal",
                       "Emergent Vegitation" = "Emergent Vegetation"))

edsm <- read_csv("data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(waterbody = recode_wb(habitat2020))

# Rip Rap: not in the model dataset, pulled from the full survey compilation.
riprap <- read_csv("data/All_Surveys_Combined_v7.3.csv",
                   show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 50000) %>%
  filter(Survey == "TPS", Edge_Type == "Riprap") %>%
  transmute(Station_Latitude, Station_Longitude, edge = "Rip Rap") %>%
  distinct()

stopifnot(!any(paste(riprap$Station_Latitude, riprap$Station_Longitude) %in%
               paste(tps$Station_Latitude, tps$Station_Longitude)))

as_pts <- function(d) st_as_sf(d, coords = c("Station_Longitude", "Station_Latitude"),
                               crs = 4326)

# One marker per sampled location. TPS StationCode is unique per tow-year, so
# every row is its own site; EDSM revisits stations, so collapse to unique sites.
tps_edge_sf <- tps %>%
  select(Station_Latitude, Station_Longitude, edge) %>%
  bind_rows(riprap) %>%
  as_pts()

tps_wb_sf <- tps %>%
  distinct(Station_Latitude, Station_Longitude, waterbody) %>%
  as_pts()

edsm_wb_sf <- edsm %>%
  distinct(StationCode, Station_Latitude, Station_Longitude, waterbody) %>%
  as_pts()

count(st_drop_geometry(tps_edge_sf), edge,      sort = TRUE)
count(st_drop_geometry(tps_wb_sf),   waterbody, sort = TRUE)
count(st_drop_geometry(edsm_wb_sf),  waterbody, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r geometry-helpers}
extent_of <- function(..., pad_x = 0.015, pad_y = 0.015) {
  bbs <- lapply(list(...), st_bbox)
  list(xlim = c(min(sapply(bbs, `[[`, "xmin")) - pad_x,
                max(sapply(bbs, `[[`, "xmax")) + pad_x),
       ylim = c(min(sapply(bbs, `[[`, "ymin")) - pad_y,
                max(sapply(bbs, `[[`, "ymax")) + pad_y))
}

# Panel height / panel width that coord_sf will enforce for a lon/lat extent.
# Used to derive the figure height so panels fill the requested width exactly.
map_aspect <- function(ext) {
  diff(ext$ylim) / (diff(ext$xlim) * cos(mean(ext$ylim) * pi / 180))
}

# Label pinned inside the upper-left corner of the panel, on an opaque white
# plate so it stays legible over water, land or markers.
corner_label <- function(ext, txt, inset_x = 0.006, inset_y = 0.012) {
  annotate("label",
           x = ext$xlim[1] + inset_x * diff(ext$xlim),
           y = ext$ylim[2] - inset_y * diff(ext$ylim),
           label = txt, hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
           size = PT_MM, fontface = "bold", colour = "black",
           fill = "white", border.colour = NA,
           label.padding = unit(1.2, "pt"), label.r = unit(0, "pt"))
}

# Hairline black frame; with zero plot margins, adjacent frames abut and read as
# a single thin divider between panels.
DIVIDER <- element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.25)

panel_theme <- function() {
  theme_void(base_size = BASE_PT) +
    theme(
      text             = element_text(size = BASE_PT),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = LAND_FILL, colour = NA),
      panel.border     = DIVIDER,
      plot.margin      = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.background  = element_blank()
    )
}
```

## Edge type — six panels, 174 mm

```{r edge-facets, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
W_EDGE   <- 174 / 25.4      # mm -> in
NCOL     <- 2
NROW     <- 3

ext_edge <- extent_of(tps_edge_sf)
H_EDGE   <- W_EDGE * map_aspect(ext_edge) * NROW / NCOL

edge_levels <- c("Natural Edge", "Emergent Vegetation", "Cut Bank",
                 "Earthen Levee", "Shoal", "Rip Rap")

# Context = the model tow locations, so the Rip Rap panel still shows where the
# rest of the survey went without adding non-model points to the other panels.
context_sf <- tps_edge_sf[tps_edge_sf$edge != "Rip Rap", ]

edge_panel <- function(lev) {
  d <- tps_edge_sf[tps_edge_sf$edge == lev, ]
  # Rip Rap is not a model level -- a black cross separates it at a glance from
  # the filled circles used for the five modelled edge types.
  marker <- if (lev == "Rip Rap") {
    geom_sf(data = d, shape = 4, colour = "black", size = 1.7, stroke = 0.6)
  } else {
    geom_sf(data = d, shape = 21, fill = pal[[lev]], colour = pal_stroke[[lev]],
            size = 1.4, stroke = 0.26)
  }
  ggplot() +
    basemap_layer() +
    geom_sf(data = context_sf, colour = "grey76", size = 0.25, shape = 16) +
    marker +
    corner_label(ext_edge, sprintf("%s (n = %d)", lev, nrow(d))) +
    coord_sf(xlim = ext_edge$xlim, ylim = ext_edge$ylim, expand = FALSE, crs = 4326) +
    panel_theme()
}

# plot_annotation() zeroes patchwork's own 5.5 pt outer margin, which would
# otherwise inset the whole assembly and reintroduce white edges.
NO_MARGIN <- plot_annotation(theme = theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)))

p_edge <- wrap_plots(lapply(edge_levels, edge_panel), ncol = NCOL) + NO_MARGIN
print(p_edge)

ggsave("output_figs/TPS_edge_type_map.pdf",  p_edge, width = W_EDGE, height = H_EDGE)
ggsave("output_figs/TPS_edge_type_map.tiff", p_edge, width = W_EDGE, height = H_EDGE,
       dpi = 600, compression = "lzw")
ggsave("output_figs/TPS_edge_type_map_preview.png", p_edge,
       width = W_EDGE, height = H_EDGE, dpi = 320)

cat(sprintf("edge figure: %.1f x %.1f mm\n", W_EDGE * 25.4, H_EDGE * 25.4))
```

## Water body type — TPS over EDSM, 84 mm

Each panel carries its own legend with its own `n`, so the counts are
unambiguous. Both panels share one extent, extended south by `LEG_CLEAR` mm so
each legend sits below the southernmost point rather than over it. The legend
width was measured off the built grob (`guide-box-inside`) rather than guessed:
the full `Name (n = ###)` form is 80.7 mm for TPS and 77.5 mm for EDSM, so it
clears 84 mm on one row.

`n` is the number of sampling locations plotted. TPS station codes are unique per
tow-year, so a TPS marker is one tow; EDSM revisits stations, so an EDSM marker
is one station (4,241 EDSM tows at 1,005 stations) — worth stating in the caption.

```{r waterbody-stack, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
W_WB      <- 84 / 25.4
LEG_CLEAR <- 6.0     # mm of empty map reserved under BOTH panels for the legend

wb_levels <- c("Shoal", "Distributary", "Terminal")

# Short display names; the data still carries the full "... Channel" labels.
short_wb <- c("Shoal" = "Shoal",
              "Distributary Channel" = "Distributary",
              "Terminal Channel"     = "Terminal")

bb_t <- st_bbox(tps_wb_sf); bb_e <- st_bbox(edsm_wb_sf)
XLIM <- c(min(bb_t["xmin"], bb_e["xmin"]) - 0.015,
          max(bb_t["xmax"], bb_e["xmax"]) + 0.015)
YMAX <- max(bb_t["ymax"], bb_e["ymax"]) + 0.015
YMIN <- min(bb_t["ymin"], bb_e["ymin"])

# Degrees of latitude per inch of panel depends only on the shared x extent, so
# mm of legend clearance converts to degrees before the panel height is known.
DEG_PER_IN <- diff(XLIM) * cos(mean(c(YMIN, YMAX)) * pi / 180) / W_WB

ext_wb <- list(xlim = unname(XLIM),
               ylim = unname(c(YMIN - (LEG_CLEAR / 25.4) * DEG_PER_IN, YMAX)))
H_WB   <- W_WB * map_aspect(ext_wb) * 2

STROKE      <- 0.14
EMPH_STROKE <- 0.30

#' @param emph level given the white-ring treatment, or NULL
wb_panel <- function(sfobj, label, size_range = c(0.55, 0.95),
                     emph = "Terminal Channel", emph_size = 1.15) {
  v      <- sfobj$waterbody
  counts <- sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE)
  lv     <- names(counts)                      # most common -> rarest
  sizes  <- setNames(seq(size_range[1], size_range[2], length.out = length(lv)), lv)
  if (!is.null(emph) && emph %in% lv) sizes[emph] <- emph_size

  # Per-panel legend labels, so each n belongs to the map above it.
  n_here <- table(recode(v, !!!short_wb))
  labs   <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n = %d)", wb_levels, n_here[wb_levels]), wb_levels)

  p <- ggplot() + basemap_layer()

  # Drawn most common first, so the rarest level ends up on top.
  for (l in lv) {
    d <- sfobj[v == l, ]
    if (identical(l, emph)) {
      p <- p + geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = short_wb[waterbody]), shape = 21,
                       colour = "white", size = sizes[[l]], stroke = EMPH_STROKE)
    } else {
      p <- p + geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = short_wb[waterbody]), shape = 21,
                       colour = pal_stroke[[l]], size = sizes[[l]], stroke = STROKE)
    }
  }

  p +
    corner_label(ext_wb, label) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(unname(pal[names(short_wb)]), short_wb),
                      breaks = wb_levels, limits = wb_levels,
                      labels = labs, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    coord_sf(xlim = ext_wb$xlim, ylim = ext_wb$ylim, expand = FALSE, crs = 4326) +
    panel_theme() +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(
      size   = 1.35,
      colour = c(pal_stroke[["Shoal"]], pal_stroke[["Distributary Channel"]], "white"),
      stroke = c(STROKE, STROKE, EMPH_STROKE)))) +
    theme(
      legend.position        = "inside",
      legend.position.inside = c(0.5, 0.010),
      legend.justification   = c(0.5, 0),
      legend.direction       = "horizontal",
      legend.background      = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      legend.key             = element_blank(),
      legend.text            = element_text(size = BASE_PT, margin = margin(l = 1, r = 3)),
      legend.key.size        = unit(6, "pt"),
      legend.key.spacing.x   = unit(0, "pt"),
      legend.margin          = margin(1.5, 2.5, 1.5, 1.5),
      legend.box.spacing     = unit(0, "pt")
    )
}

p_wb <- wb_panel(tps_wb_sf, "TPS") / wb_panel(edsm_wb_sf, "EDSM") + NO_MARGIN
print(p_wb)

ggsave("output_figs/TPS_EDSM_waterbody_map.pdf",  p_wb, width = W_WB, height = H_WB)
ggsave("output_figs/TPS_EDSM_waterbody_map.tiff", p_wb, width = W_WB, height = H_WB,
       dpi = 600, compression = "lzw")
ggsave("output_figs/TPS_EDSM_waterbody_map_preview.png", p_wb,
       width = W_WB, height = H_WB, dpi = 600)

cat(sprintf("water body figure: %.1f x %.1f mm\n", W_WB * 25.4, H_WB * 25.4))
cat(sprintf("clearance %.1f mm | lowest point %.4f | panel floor %.4f\n",
            LEG_CLEAR, YMIN, ext_wb$ylim[1]))
```
